content:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp spikes in sentiment (e.g., +1.00 followed by +1.00), leading to overcorrection; dampen peak forecasts.
- If 3–5 consecutive days of high sentiment (≥0.67) precede forecast, model often fails to mean-revert; apply mild downward bias to avoid overbought bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag behind true price by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day trend, not just 30d average.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model often holds high forecast; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment drop.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending, model underreacts; add 0.3–0.7% upward bias to capture momentum.
- Avoid forecasting based solely on 30d average; incorporate sentiment-weighted recent 7–14 day mean for better alignment with true price.
